div.p: * Workloads are considered "actively hostile" and account is "assumed compromised".
* Runs in a dedicated cloud account for hostile workloads - full account-level segmentation from trusted workloads.
* VPC firewall rules on Node Pools enforce internet egress policies outside of the cluster.

* Cluster and account are fully audited to avoid any known cloud account privilege escalation paths from the cluster - so we can still rely on VPC level segmentation rules and account-level security and detection.
* Shared responsibility model puts Cloud 0-days in Cloud Provider's scope - not our responsibility.

We expect suspicious activity there (e.g. processes spawned, but not cluster k8s attacks)
* Pay special attention to anomalies in Restricted Nodes in Hostile Cluster - this is egress/privesc path for hostile agents.
* Canaries are an indicator of compromise or an agent gone rogue and require immediate attention.
